# How MSF is responding to the war in Gaza

The humanitarian crisis in Gaza remains catastrophic, with ongoing attacks, limited supplies, and dire living conditions.

### Israel blocks crucial supplies from entering Gaza, putting thousands at risk

**August 12, 2026 —** Israeli authorities continue to restrict the entry of engine oil and spare parts into Gaza, Palestine, increasing the risk of death and severe illness for thousands of Palestinians. These critical supplies are essential to keep hospital generators, ambulances, water pumps, and water trucks running.

MSF calls on Israeli authorities to immediately lift the blockade on Gaza and allow unhindered entry of all medical, humanitarian, and commercial supplies needed to respond to Palestinians' immense needs.

[Read more](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/israel-blocks-crucial-supplies-entering-gaza-putting-thousands-risk "Israel blocks crucial supplies from entering Gaza, putting thousands at risk")

Israeli forces’ all-out war on Gaza has systematically destroyed the conditions necessary for life in the Strip — attacking hospitals, striking tented camps and fragile shelters, destroying vital civilian infrastructure, and choking off access to food, water, medicines, and other basic needs for survival. No one is spared.

Since October 2023, more than 73,000 [Palestinians](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/where-we-work/palestine "Palestine") have been killed and over 173,000 wounded. Nearly 2,300 health and humanitarian workers have been killed, including 15 of our own Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) [colleagues](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/remembering-our-colleagues-killed-gaza "Remembering our colleagues killed in Gaza"). It will take decades to rebuild and recover, and for many Palestinians, the physical and emotional wounds will last a lifetime.

Despite the [ceasefire agreement](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/msf-denounces-ongoing-bloodshed-gaza "MSF denounces ongoing bloodshed in Gaza ") in October 2025, violence and killings of Palestinians continue daily. Israel maintains its blockade, preventing sufficient aid from entering the Strip, depriving people of the essentials they need to live, and prolonging this genocide.

Now, more than ever, Palestinians need more humanitarian aid, not less. We reiterate our call for unhindered access to independent, impartial humanitarian aid in Palestine.

## How we're responding in Gaza

### What does MSF do in Gaza?

MSF has over 1,430 staff working in Gaza's health facilities, including our two field hospitals in Deir al-Balah and our clinics in Gaza City and Khan Younis. Our teams provide surgical care, wound and burn care, [malnutrition](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/five-things-know-about-starvation-gaza "Five things to know about the starvation in Gaza") screening and treatment, [maternal and pediatric care](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/devastating-impact-israels-manufactured-malnutrition-crisis-gaza "The devastating impact of Israel’s manufactured malnutrition crisis in Gaza"), [physiotherapy](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/how-3d-masks-are-helping-heal-facial-burns-gaza "How 3D masks are helping to heal facial burns in Gaza"), vaccination, mental health support, [water and sanitation](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/israel-must-stop-using-water-weapon-collective-punishment-gaza "Israel must stop using water as a weapon of collective punishment in Gaza") support, and care for non-communicable diseases, among other services. We are also assisting [medical evacuations](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/drop-ocean-witnessing-gazas-medical-evacuations "A drop in the ocean: Witnessing Gaza’s medical evacuations") and providing evacuees with [rehabilitative care](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/we-share-same-pain-peer-support-war-wounded-patients-middle-east "We share the same pain: Peer support for war-wounded patients in the Middle East") at our reconstructive surgery hospital in Amman, [Jordan](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/where-we-work/jordan "Jordan").

#### Medical services

MSF teams have worked in health facilities across Gaza, including its largest hospitals and our own clinics and field hospital. However, due to extremely volatile conditions on the ground — such as [attacks on health facilities](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/focus/attacks-health-care "Attacks on health care") and recurrent [evacuation orders](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/israeli-displacement-orders-gaza-are-psychological-warfare "Israeli displacement orders in Gaza are psychological warfare") — our teams have had to move from facility to facility and continually adapt our activities.

Despite the so-called ceasefire, MSF teams continue to treat patients suffering from blast injuries, fragment wounds, and blunt trauma caused by explosions and gunshot wounds, including those shot by Israeli forces near the shifting “yellow line.”

As of May 2026, MSF is running or supporting health services in more than 10 locations across north, south, and central Gaza. We currently support two public hospitals, Nasser and Al-Helou, while supporting four general health care centers and working in five clinics and four medical points. We also run one field hospital and support another in the Deir al-Balah area.

#### Medical evacuations

MSF supports [medical evacuations](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/medical-evacuation-gaza-thousands-need-care-no-longer-available-strip "Medical evacuation from Gaza: Thousands need care no longer available in the Strip ") for patients in need of specialized care no longer available in Gaza due to Israeli forces’ decimation of its health system. To date, MSF has supported 147 medical evacuations. Sixty-six of these patients were [evacuated to Jordan](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/long-road-recovery-gazas-war-wounded-children "The long road to recovery for Gaza’s war-wounded children") for treatment at MSF’s reconstructive surgery hospital in Amman; the remainder were evacuated to Spain, [Switzerland](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/drop-ocean-witnessing-gazas-medical-evacuations "A drop in the ocean: Witnessing Gaza’s medical evacuations"), and other countries in partnership with governing authorities.

But this is only a drop in the ocean: More than 18,500 Palestinians require medical evacuation, including children and elderly patients with severe burns and fractures, amputations, congenital anomalies, and other serious conditions. A clear, predictable medical evacuation system must be established urgently — with full respect to patients’ right to a safe, voluntary, and dignified return to Gaza.

#### Water and sanitation support

Water and sanitation is a significant part of MSF’s response in Gaza. We carry out water trucking activities, establish distribution points, and provide technical support to desalination plants. In 2025, MSF distributed over 1.1 million gallons of water across Gaza. In May 2026, MSF purified 17,114,122 gallons of water through reverse osmosis and distributed 15,506,371 gallons.

Lack of water is life-threatening and can contribute to health issues like diarrhea, jaundice, and scabies. Dehydration can be lethal and also makes it harder to recover from other diseases.

Gaza has no independent means of producing drinkable water, as its groundwater is too salty or contaminated by sewage and agricultural chemicals to be fit for human consumption. Israeli forces have [decimated](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/water-being-used-weapon-war-gaza "Water is being used as a weapon of war in Gaza") the water network. And with the establishment of the yellow line, key water infrastructure like boreholes are dangerous to reach as they are located within or close to the militarized zone.

Israeli authorities have also blocked the entry of key water production supplies, leaving authorization requests for items like pumps, spare parts, and tanks pending for months. Since January, one-third of our requests to bring in critical water and sanitation supplies have been rejected or left unanswered.

![Map of MSF presence in Gaza](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/sites/default/files/styles/large_image_1340_893/public/MSF-gaza-9.png?itok=0jryHjv7)

Between the October 10, 2025 — when the ceasefire went into effect — through April 2026, MSF provided:

- Care for **49,089** trauma cases
- Outpatient consultations for **594,206** people
- Care for **17,974** diarrhea cases
- **14,412** surgical procedures
- Inpatient admission for **27,684** people
- **7,515** deliveries
- **41,199** individual mental health sessions
- **1,105** routine vaccinations
- **17,114,122** gallons of water produced through reverse osmosis
- **15,506,371** gallons of water through distributions

### How has Israel’s deregistration of NGOs impacted MSF operations?

Earlier this year, [Israel barred MSF and other major nongovernmental organizations](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/israels-grave-threat-withhold-ngo-registration "Israel’s grave threat to withhold NGO registration") from working in Gaza and the West Bank, leaving hundreds of thousands of Palestinians unable to access lifesaving health care, water, and other essential services.

Since our international staff were [forced to leave](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/msf-will-not-share-staff-information-about-its-colleagues-palestine-israeli-authorities "MSF will not share staff information about its colleagues in Palestine with Israeli authorities") Gaza at the end of February, MSF has been operating with about 1,430 Palestinian staff in Gaza (registered under the Palestinian Authority), with international staff providing remote support from Amman. Israeli authorities have also [blocked MSF from bringing supplies](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/aid-and-supplies-are-still-being-blocked-entering-gaza "Aid and supplies are still being blocked from entering Gaza") into Palestine since January. Stocks of medication, medical equipment, and engine oil — essential for generators keeping babies in incubators alive — are critically depleted. This engineered scarcity has made it impossible to meet basic needs.

MSF will continue to provide medical humanitarian care and bear witness to the suffering of the Palestinian people for as long as possible. We are working urgently to preserve access to health care for our patients in an increasingly constrained environment.

### What are the medical needs MSF is seeing in Gaza?

The medical needs in Gaza are immense and urgent, not only for people wounded or burned in strikes but for children with malnutrition, pregnant women who are about to deliver, the elderly, and people with chronic diseases. At the same time, the provision of care has become even more challenging due to the systematic dismantling of Gaza’s health system, with repeated attacks by Israeli forces on health facilities and personnel, as well as shortages of essential supplies including vital medicines and medical equipment. The core medical needs our teams are seeing on the ground include:

##### Malnutrition

On August 22, 2025, the United Nations-coordinated Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) system officially declared famine in Gaza governorate, in the north of the Gaza Strip, indicating a severe risk of malnutrition, with children being the most vulnerable. Israel’s manufactured malnutrition crisis in Gaza had a devastating impact on pregnant and breastfeeding women, newborns, and infants under 6 months old during periods of intense hostilities and siege: Between late 2024 and early 2026, our teams at four health facilities [recorded higher levels of miscarriage as well as prematurity and mortality](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/devastating-impact-israels-manufactured-malnutrition-crisis-gaza "The devastating impact of Israel’s manufactured malnutrition crisis in Gaza") among infants born to mothers affected by malnutrition during their pregnancy.

##### War wounds, crush injuries, and burn care

Many patients require [care for war wounds](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/focus/care-in-conflict-zones "Delivering care in a conflict zone"), crush injuries, and burns sustained in bombings and other attacks by Israeli forces. In 2025, MSF teams saw an increase in the number of patients with [burn injuries](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/no-relief-no-chance-recovery-gazas-burn-patients "No relief, no chance of recovery for Gaza’s burn patients") — most of them children. Many of these children were burned by bomb blasts; others by boiling water or fuel used for cooking or heating in makeshift shelters.

##### Infections and diseases

Infections resulting from poorly treated wounds are a growing concern, driven by the difficulty wounded people face accessing care and follow-up, shortages of supplies, and lack of access to hygiene. There is also a high risk of infectious diseases including diarrhea, acute respiratory infections, [skin infections](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/conditions-gaza-are-causing-severe-health-issues-palestinian-children-and-babies "Conditions in Gaza are causing severe health issues for Palestinian children and babies"), and hepatitis due to overcrowding and poor hygienic conditions in camps where displaced people are sheltering, and shortages of medicines and medical supplies.

##### Pediatric care

Even before the current war started, many years of instability had already taken a toll on the physical and mental health of [Gaza’s children](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/most-dangerous-place-world-be-child "The most dangerous place in the world to be a child"), leaving many with life-changing injuries, amputated limbs, and the trauma of losing parents and other loved ones along with their homes and schools. Children are also especially vulnerable to various [health risks](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/focus/child-health-initiatives "Children’s health") arising from insufficient access to water, food, and warm shelter.

##### Maternal care

Pregnant women in Gaza have been forced to navigate [severe obstacles](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/maha-gave-birth-public-bathroom-her-story-not-unique-gaza "Maha gave birth in a public bathroom. Her story is not unique in Gaza.") to reach medical facilities for prenatal care or delivery, including traveling dangerous routes amid fighting and without safe transportation, which can delay access to care and increase the risk of complications. Those able to reach a hospital often find them without capacity, and end up giving birth in in plastic tents or public spaces; others must return to their makeshift shelters mere hours after undergoing cesarean sections. To date, MSF teams have [assisted](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/medical-issues/maternal-health "Maternal health") more than 21000 deliveries in Gaza — 1 in 3 births.

##### Humanitarian aid and medical supplies

Throughout the war, our teams operated under a severe shortage of medical supplies such as anesthetics, pediatric antibiotics, and medicines for chronic conditions like epilepsy, hypertension, and [diabetes](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/medical-issues/diabetes "Diabetes") as a result of the blockade. Staff have been forced to ration medications and even turn some patients away because they don’t have the proper tools to treat them.

### How is MSF responding in the West Bank?

Since October 2023, Palestinians in the West Bank have faced an escalation of violence by Israeli forces and settlers, including movement restrictions, obstructions of health care, demolition of homes, and forced displacement. Since October 2023, at least 1,100 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank, including at least 239 children, according to [OCHA](https://www.ochaopt.org/data/casualties "(opens in a new window)").

MSF calls for an immediate end to forced displacement and military aggression against Palestinians in the West Bank.

#### MSF activities in the West Bank

Our teams in the West Bank are expanding efforts to reach communities where people are unable to access care, such as the north of the occupied territory and remote areas such as [Masafer Yatta](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/they-shoot-kill-settler-violence-west-bank "“They shoot to kill”: Settler violence in the West Bank") in the south. We aim to bolster the local [emergency response capacity](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/stop-bleed-palestinians-tulkarem-learn-how-respond-medical-emergencies "Stop the bleed:  Palestinians in Tulkarem learn how to respond to medical emergencies"), including by training health care workers and teaching community members how to provide first aid in the event that they are unable to reach care when it’s needed. We also distribute relief items for displaced people.

In Nablus and Hebron, MSF teams are providing [psychosocial support](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/hebron-picture-life-under-violence-and-occupation "In Hebron, a picture of life under violence and occupation"); care for [sexual and gender-based violence](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/medical-issues/sexual-and-gender-based-violence "Sexual and gender-based violence"); and psychological, emergency, and first response training. In Hebron, we run mobile clinics providing general health care, sexual and reproductive health care, and mental health support.

### Is MSF providing medical care in Israel?

MSF does not currently run medical programs in Israel but offered its support to Israeli hospitals treating large numbers of casualties following the Hamas attacks on October 7, 2023. We focus on filling the greatest gaps in health care, and Israel has strong emergency and health systems.

### What does it mean to be an independent and impartial medical humanitarian organization?

MSF provides medical care to anyone who needs it, regardless of race, religion, or political affiliation. As an organization, we focus on filling the greatest gaps in health care.

To facilitate our humanitarian and medical work, we speak to all parties to the conflict to request safe, rapid, and unimpeded access to civilians who require medical care and to ensure the safety and security of our staff. Our independence and impartiality are essential to our work in all the places we operate across the globe. We also believe that the principles of impartiality and neutrality are not synonymous with silence. When the world turns its back on crises, we are duty-bound to raise our voices and speak out on behalf of our patients. Our decision to do so is always guided by our mission to do no harm, preserve respect and dignity, and protect life and health.

## Dancing his way out of the hospital in Gaza

Witness the joyful moment a patient was discharged from MSF’s Al-Zawayda Field Hospital after regaining his mobility and independent movement.
